note: What to think of before a planned stay in hospital. Written for this skill as general, practical advice: it is no hospital's own list, and it says nothing about what to do before a procedure. The ward's instructions come first.
pack_note: general advice, written for this skill. If the ward sends a list of its own, that one comes first
pack: an identity document, and the referral or the admission letter
the medicines taken at home, in their own packs, unless the ward says to leave them
glasses, hearing aids and dentures, with their cases, and a name on each
nightwear, slippers that grip, something warm, and a wash bag
a phone and its charger; leave valuables at home
something to read or to listen to, and earplugs
the name and number of the person to ring
ask_note: questions for the ward or the admissions office, before the day
ask: when to arrive, where to report, and how long the stay is expected to last
whether to eat, drink or take the usual medicines beforehand, and until when: only the hospital can answer that
which of the usual medicines to bring, and which to leave at home
the visiting hours, and who may be told how things are going
what happens on the day of going home: who collects, what is handed over, and who to ring if something is wrong afterwards
bring: a list of every medicine and supplement, with strengths and times
allergies, and what happened each time, written down
recent results, discharge letters, and the names of the doctors involved
the person's own questions, written down, with room for the answers
rule: what to do before a procedure (eating, drinking, medicines) is the hospital's to say and nobody else's. Where its instructions and this list differ, the hospital's stand
